title: The Last Emperor (1987) by Bernardo Bertolucci is a beautiful film

commenti.body:
Do you have any thoughts as to why some people consider it a weaker Best Picture winner? A few examples can be seen [here](https://www.simbasible.com/the-last-emperor-movie-review/) and [here](https://ew.com/gallery/most-overrated-best-picture-winners/).

Is it just a hype backlash? A perception of the epic historical drama as an outdated genre?

While generally critically acclaimed, it did get some fairly scathing reviews when it came out:

* Pauline Kael writes that the film's locations, cinematography and art direction "aren't in the service of anything in particular and they make no real mark on you." She writes that it has a "dubious message" and that "Bertolucci makes pretty pictorial music, but two hours and forty-six minutes is a long time for a movie to dance."
* Vincent Canby calls it an "elegant travel brochure," one politically and aesthetically compromised by the filmmakers' collaboration with the Chinese government.
* Michael Sragow compares it to *Masterpiece Theater*, writing that "The moviemakers sacrifice any deep involvement with their anti-hero for a flatly pretty presentation."

My two cents: it's not an all-time favorite of mine, but it certainly is a visually spectacular film with a handful of unforgettable images and scenes, especially the early meeting with the dowager empress. Looking at its Oscar competition, I really don't think that any of *Broadcast News*, *Fatal Attraction*, *Hope and Glory* or *Moonstruck* are really remembered as canonical classic films. I'd be surprised if they shared a *Sight and Sound* vote between them.
